yt_title: Why Doesn't Water Fall Out Of An Upside Down Glass? #Shorts
desc: Why doesn't water fall out of an upside down glass with a card on top? Air pressure pushes up on the card harder than the water pushes down. A simple physics DIY. New fizzy fact every day on Fruit Soda.
caption: Upside down glass, no spill 😮 Do it over a sink! Comment A or B: does air push up or down? Follow for a fact every day.

lines.text: Why doesn't water fall out of an upside down glass?
Fill a glass to the brim and lay a flat card on top.
Hold the card, flip the glass, then let go of the card.
The card stays. Air pushes up on it with about ten newtons on every square centimetre.
That upward push is much more than the weight of the water pushing down.
Air pressure is invisible but strong. Now watch the flip again.
